While meth use is often portrayed in television shows and movies, these are not always accurate depictions of what occurs when someone is struggling with an addiction.

What is Meth?

Meth is a highly addictive stimulant that is made from several chemicals. When someone uses meth, their Central Nervous System is impacted. While meth can be produced in a lab, a large portion of the meth being used in the United States is not being made here. Mistakes made while producing meth can lead to an explosion, and the individuals who make meth can have lasting consequences from their exposure to the common chemicals used.

What Are the Signs of Meth Use?
Since meth is a stimulant, individuals who use it can appear similar to those who use other amphetamines and cocaine. Signs and symptoms commonly experienced by those who use meth include:
Increased physical activity
Decrease in appetite and weight loss
Increased breathing
Irregular heartbeat
Increased blood pressure
Paranoia and hallucinogens
Confusion
Scratching, itching, and scabs on the body
An overdose can occur when someone ingests too much meth. An overdose is a medical emergency, and the individual needs medical intervention as soon as possible.

How Does Meth Impact the Body?

There are several ways that meth affects a person’s body. Similar to other substances, when ingested, a person’s brain releases a naturally occurring chemical in our brain called dopamine. Dopamine is a chemical involved in the reward system of our brain, which allows us to feel pleasure. Because of this, individuals often continue using it to experience the same high that they did before.
Additionally, meth can have an impact on a person’s peripheral nervous system, immune system, and gastrointestinal system.

What Are the Symptoms of Meth Withdrawal?

Your experience with meth withdrawal will be dependent on several factors, including the severity of your use, method of use, and the purity of the substances used. With that being said, symptoms that can arise include:
Mood swings
Psychosis
Suicidal thoughts and ideation
Chills
Dehydration
Inability to feel pleasure
Cravings
